attribution.note: Zitron's own authorial sentence in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'This' refers to the hallucinations described just before. The normalisation keeps both parts: reliance is limited, and the problem grows with task complexity.

contract.note: The plain reading (material loss of dependable completion that gets worse with complexity) is ordinary. The Feb 1–19, 2024 window was chosen by the evaluator, and complexity and severity have no thresholds, so interpretation shapes any result.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own Sora page says entities can spontaneously appear in scenes with many entities. That is a qualitative company disclosure about one model. It gives no controlled error rates and no measure of reliance, so under the contract it cannot settle severity or generality.

reviews.rationale: The only item is a company's qualitative admission about one model, consistent with the complexity part. The packet has no controlled evaluation that varies complexity, separates out hallucinations, and measures the effect on reliable completion in the period. The contract's support condition is not met and nothing contradicts the claim, so it is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own inference ('In plain English...') drawn from the McKinsey figures he cites.

semantics.note: Faithful, and it keeps 'does not seem'. But the sentence is a tentative, hedged inference, not a firm observation. Under policy, hedged language of this kind is not scored.

contract.note: The contract itself calls the sentence a tentative inference, yet it applies a plain reading, which policy reserves for firm language. It also has to supply the metric (organisation-wide EBIT), the period (2023) and a prevalence threshold that the speaker never gave.

evidence.note: McKinsey 2023 report covering AI in general and earnings for 2022. It does not isolate generative AI or 2023.

McKinsey early-2024 survey (published before the evaluation date) reports function-level generative AI revenue and cost gains in 2023, mostly small. These are gross function-level figures, not organisation-wide EBIT.

reviews.rationale: 'Doesn't seem to be' is a hedged, tentative inference comparable to 'I suspect', so it is not scored. Even on the contract's reading, the packet has only function-level gross benefit data and nothing on organisation-wide generative AI EBIT, so the outcome would be unresolved.

attribution.note: The topic sentence is Zitron's own. He cites Big Technology for the data and endorses it.

semantics.note: The claim is that indications of lost interest exist. Adding ChatGPT traffic stagnation or decline reflects the supporting sentence that follows.

contract.note: Testing whether the cited usage indicators existed (web visits below the May 2023 peak) is a fair, ordinary reading of 'there are indications'.

evidence.note: TheWrap (Feb 16, 2024), citing Similarweb: January 2024 web visits of 1.6B were 11% below the May 2023 peak, with growth stagnant since mid-2023. Countervailing point: US app users rose from 4.3M to 6.3M.

reviews.rationale: Contemporaneous reporting that names Similarweb as the source confirms that web traffic was below its peak and stagnant through January 2024, which meets the support condition. App growth weakens the passage's 'both mobile and web' aside. It does not negate the narrower claim that indications existed.

semantics.note: The normalisation keeps 'almost every dollar' and 'eventually shared'. It drops 'guarantees' and 'any', but the scope is essentially the same.

contract.note: Reading 'shared' as some portion reaching Amazon, Microsoft or Google, directly or indirectly, is a fair reading drawn from the surrounding text. Using Q4 2023 is reasonable.

evidence.note: Synergy reports the top three held 67% of Q4 2023 cloud infrastructure services. That measures market concentration, not how much AI-product spending ends up paying these firms.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no payment-chain data showing what share of AI-product spending reaches the named firms. Cloud market share is a different metric, so it neither supports nor contradicts the near-universal claim. The outcome is unresolved.
